$comment: Machine-readable form of the state machines in docs/protocol/SPEC-0.1.md sections 3-7.
This file is the artifact a second implementation implements against; the prose
document explains WHY each rule exists, this one says exactly WHAT it is.
state-machines.mjs enforces three-way agreement between this file, the SQL
migrations, and the spec prose, so none of the three can rot independently.

purchases.status.note: escrow_held is read as a sold state but never written -- see D9.1.

delivery_referee_reports.verdict.note: Uses 'accepted' where sandbox_reports uses 'approved' -- see D9.5.

disputes.decision.note: 'manual_review' is the at-rest marker on an unresolved dispute, not a resolution -- see the disputes_terminal_decision_executable invariant. 'split' was withdrawn in 000028; it was recordable and unexecutable.

invariants.why: Automation may only resolve a dispute that is both low-risk and clearly evidenced. Enforced at the storage layer so no later code path can forget it.

A dispute that has stopped moving must carry a decision the payout path can act on. Without this, 'manual_review' -- the marker meaning nobody has ruled -- could be frozen into a terminal state, stranding the escrow exactly the way 'split' did. Enforced at the storage layer because more than one path writes this row.
An unbound agent holds no operator and always has a live claim path; any bound state holds an operator. Neither half can be represented alone.

absentByDesign.why: Commission was once pinned to exactly 1200 bps. Migration 000018 dropped that in favour of a stored policy bounded by product_versions_commission_bps_check. If this constraint ever comes back, A5.3 ('a stored policy value, not a constant') is false and the spec must change with it.

appendOnly.why: Money movement is recorded, never edited. Direction is carried by entry_type, not by mutating a row.
